title: MFS API Catalog - All Services
text: Meridian Financial Services API Catalog. Welcome to the MFS API developer portal. This catalog lists all available APIs for internal and partner integration. Production APIs. Payment Gateway API v2 (Production) - Full payment lifecycle management including card tokenization, payment processing, refunds, and settlement. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/payments/v2. Owner: Payments Core (Arjun Deshmukh). Service: mfs-payment-gateway on mfs-pay-pod-01. Authentication: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token. Rate limit: 1,000 rpm (POST), 5,000 rpm (GET). Fraud Scoring API v2 (Production) - Real-time transaction fraud scoring with ML model predictions and AML rule evaluation. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/fraud/v2. Owner: Fraud and Risk (Priya Natarajan). Service: mfs-fraud-engine on mfs-fraud-pod-01. Authentication: mTLS with service certificates. Rate limit: 2,000 rpm. Token Vault API v1 (Production) - Card tokenization and detokenization service for PCI-compliant card data handling. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/tokens/v1. Owner: Payments Core (Elena Volkov). Service: mfs-payment-gateway on mfs-pay-pod-01. Authentication: mTLS with service certificates + HSM authorization. Rate limit: 3,000 rpm. Settlement API v1 (Production) - Batch settlement processing and reconciliation for completed payment transactions. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/settlements/v1. Owner: Payments Core (Sarah Chen). Service: mfs-payment-gateway on mfs-pay-pod-01. Authentication: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token. Rate limit: 500 rpm. AML Engine API v1 (Production) - Anti-money laundering rule evaluation and suspicious activity reporting. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/aml/v1. Owner: Fraud and Risk (Carlos Rivera). Service: mfs-fraud-engine on mfs-fraud-pod-01. Authentication: mTLS with service certificates. Rate limit: 1,000 rpm. API Standards. All APIs follow OpenAPI 3.0 specification. Versioning: URL-based major versioning (v1, v2). Error format: RFC 7807 Problem Details. Pagination: cursor-based using next_cursor parameter. All timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC format. All monetary amounts in minor units (cents). Getting Started. Request API access through your squad lead. API keys are provisioned via api.mfs.internal/admin. Service certificates for mTLS are issued from vault.mfs.internal. See individual API documentation for endpoint details and examples.

title: Payment Gateway API v2 - Swagger Documentation
text: Payment Gateway API v2. OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Payment Gateway. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/payments/v2. Service: mfs-payment-gateway deployed on mfs-pay-pod-01. Database: mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal. Service account: svc-payment-api. Endpoints. POST /payments - Create a new payment. Request body: {amount: integer (minor units), currency: string (ISO 4217), card_token: string, customer_id: string, description: string, idempotency_key: string}. Response 201: {payment_id: string, status: 'pending'|'authorized'|'captured'|'failed', amount: integer, currency: string, created_at: string, fraud_score: number}. The endpoint first calls the fraud scoring API at /fraud/v2/score to evaluate the transaction risk. If fraud_score exceeds the threshold (0.85), the payment is declined. Card tokens are generated by the Token Vault API. Events are published to the txn-events Kafka topic. GET /payments/{payment_id} - Retrieve a specific payment by ID. Response 200: Full payment object including status, amount, currency, card_token (masked), customer_id, fraud_score, processor_response, created_at, updated_at. GET /payments - List payments with filtering and pagination. Query parameters: customer_id, status, currency, from_date, to_date, cursor, limit (max 100). Response 200: {payments: Payment[], next_cursor: string, total_count: integer}. POST /payments/{payment_id}/refund - Initiate a refund for a completed payment. Request body: {amount: integer (partial refund amount, optional), reason: string}. Response 201: {refund_id: string, payment_id: string, amount: integer, status: 'pending'|'completed'|'failed', created_at: string}. Refund events are published to the refund-requests Kafka topic. GET /payments/{payment_id}/transactions - List all transactions for a payment. Response 200: {transactions: Transaction[], count: integer}. Each transaction includes type (authorization, capture, refund, chargeback), amount, status, and processor_response. Schemas. Payment: {payment_id, amount, currency, status, card_token, customer_id, fraud_score, description, processor_response, idempotency_key, created_at, updated_at}. PaymentStatus enum: pending, authorized, captured, declined, failed, refunded, partially_refunded. Currency: ISO 4217 three-letter codes. Supported: USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY. Transaction: {txn_id, payment_id, type, amount, status, processor_response, created_at}. Error Responses. 400 Bad Request: Invalid request body or parameters. 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid bearer token. 403 Forbidden: Insufficient permissions. 404 Not Found: Payment not found. 409 Conflict: Duplicate idempotency key with different payload. 422 Unprocessable Entity: Business rule violation (e.g., refund exceeds original amount). 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded. 500 Internal Server Error: Unexpected server error.

title: Fraud Scoring API v2 - Swagger Documentation
text: Fraud Scoring API v2. OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Fraud Scoring Engine. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/fraud/v2. Service: mfs-fraud-engine deployed on mfs-fraud-pod-01. Database: mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal. Service account: svc-fraud-engine. ML Model: fraud-xgb-v4.2 (production), fraud-xgb-v4.3 (canary 5%). Endpoints. POST /score - Score a transaction for fraud risk. Request body: {txn_id: string, amount: integer, currency: string, card_token: string, customer_id: string, merchant_id: string, merchant_category: string, ip_address: string, shipping_address: object, billing_address: object}. Response 200: {score_id: string, txn_id: string, ml_score: number (0.0-1.0), rule_score: number (0.0-1.0), final_score: number (0.0-1.0), risk_level: string, signals: Signal[], model_version: string, latency_ms: integer}. The scoring pipeline: 1) Extract features via FeatureExtractor.build_feature_vector, 2) ML prediction via ModelServing.predict, 3) Rule evaluation via FraudScorer.evaluate_rules (includes AML check), 4) Signal aggregation via FraudScorer.aggregate_signals. Score published to fraud-scores Kafka topic. SLA: p99 latency under 200ms. GET /score/{score_id} - Retrieve a specific fraud score. Response 200: Full score object with signals breakdown. GET /scores - List fraud scores with filtering. Query parameters: txn_id, customer_id, risk_level, min_score, max_score, from_date, to_date, cursor, limit. Response 200: {scores: FraudScore[], next_cursor: string}. POST /report - Report a confirmed fraud case for model feedback. Request body: {txn_id: string, fraud_type: string, description: string, reported_by: string}. Response 201: {report_id: string, status: 'received'}. Feedback is used in the weekly model retraining pipeline. Schemas. FraudScore: {score_id, txn_id, ml_score, rule_score, final_score, risk_level, signals, model_version, created_at}. Signal: {signal_type, signal_value, weight, description}. Signal types: velocity_anomaly, amount_anomaly, geo_risk, device_fingerprint, merchant_risk, aml_flag. Risk Levels. low (0.0-0.3): Approve automatically. medium (0.3-0.6): Approve with enhanced monitoring. high (0.6-0.85): Require additional verification. critical (0.85-1.0): Decline and flag for review.

title: Token Vault API v1 - Swagger Documentation
text: Token Vault API v1. OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Token Vault. PCI DSS Level 1 compliant card tokenization service. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/tokens/v1. Service: mfs-payment-gateway deployed on mfs-pay-pod-01 (tokenization module). HSM integration: hsm-gateway.mfs.internal:8443. Service account: svc-payment-api. Endpoints. POST /tokenize - Tokenize a card number. Request body: {pan: string (card number), expiry_month: integer, expiry_year: integer, cardholder_name: string}. Response 201: {token: string (UUID format), card_last_four: string, card_brand: string, expires_at: string}. The PAN is encrypted via HSMClient.encrypt before storage. Original PAN is never stored in any MFS database. Token is stored in mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal. All tokenization events are logged to mfs_audit_db via AuditLogger.log_event. POST /detokenize - Retrieve original card data (restricted access). Request body: {token: string, purpose: string, requester_id: string}. Response 200: {pan: string (decrypted), expiry_month: integer, expiry_year: integer, cardholder_name: string}. This endpoint requires elevated permissions and HSM authorization. Every detokenization call is logged as an audit event. Access is restricted to svc-payment-api for payment processing only. POST /rotate - Rotate a token (create new token for same card). Request body: {old_token: string}. Response 200: {new_token: string, old_token_expires_at: string}. Old token remains valid for 24 hours to allow in-flight transactions to complete. HSMClient.generate_key creates a new encryption key for the rotated token. GET /tokens/{token_id}/metadata - Get token metadata without exposing card data. Response 200: {token: string, card_last_four: string, card_brand: string, created_at: string, last_used_at: string, status: string}. Security. All endpoints require mTLS authentication with service certificates from vault.mfs.internal. Detokenization requires additional HSM-backed authorization. All operations are logged to mfs_audit_db for PCI DSS compliance. Card data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM via HSM-managed keys. Schemas. Token: {token, card_last_four, card_brand, created_at, expires_at, status}. TokenStatus enum: active, expired, revoked, rotated.

title: Settlement API v1 - Swagger Documentation
text: Settlement API v1. OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Settlement Service. Batch settlement processing and reconciliation for completed payment transactions. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/settlements/v1. Service: mfs-payment-gateway deployed on mfs-pay-pod-01 (settlement module). Database: mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal (settlements table). Service account: svc-payment-api. Endpoints. POST /batches - Create a new settlement batch. Request body: {batch_date: string (ISO date), processor_id: string, include_currencies: string[] (optional)}. Response 201: {batch_id: string, batch_date: string, transaction_count: integer, total_amount: integer, currency: string, status: 'created'}. Batches are created by aggregating all captured transactions for the given date. Batch creation publishes a settlement-batch-created event to the payment-status Kafka topic. GET /batches/{batch_id} - Retrieve a settlement batch. Response 200: {batch_id, batch_date, transaction_count, total_amount, currency, status, processor_response, created_at, settled_at, reconciled_at}. GET /batches - List settlement batches. Query parameters: status, from_date, to_date, processor_id, cursor, limit. Response 200: {batches: Settlement[], next_cursor: string}. POST /batches/{batch_id}/reconcile - Reconcile a settlement batch against processor records. Request body: {processor_total: integer, processor_count: integer, discrepancy_threshold: number}. Response 200: {batch_id: string, reconciliation_status: 'matched'|'discrepancy'|'error', our_total: integer, processor_total: integer, difference: integer, mismatched_transactions: string[]}. Reconciliation discrepancies above threshold trigger an alert to the payments-oncall PagerDuty schedule. Schemas. Settlement: {batch_id, batch_date, transaction_count, total_amount, currency, status, processor_id, processor_response, created_at, settled_at, reconciled_at}. SettlementStatus enum: created, submitted, settled, reconciled, discrepancy, failed.

title: AML Engine API v1 - Swagger Documentation
text: AML Engine API v1. OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the MFS Anti-Money Laundering Engine. Rule-based AML evaluation and suspicious activity reporting. Base URL: https://api-gateway.mfs.internal/aml/v1. Service: mfs-fraud-engine deployed on mfs-fraud-pod-01 (AML module). Database: mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal (aml_alerts table). Service account: svc-fraud-engine. Endpoints. POST /evaluate - Evaluate a transaction against AML rules. Request body: {txn_id: string, customer_id: string, amount: integer, currency: string, merchant_id: string, merchant_category: string, counterparty_info: object}. Response 200: {evaluation_id: string, txn_id: string, rules_triggered: Rule[], risk_score: number, suspicious: boolean, alert_created: boolean}. The AMLRuleEngine evaluates structuring detection, rapid movement patterns, high-risk geography, and unusual merchant activity. If suspicious, an alert is created in mfs_fraud_db and published to the aml-alerts Kafka topic. GET /alerts - List AML alerts. Query parameters: status (open, under_review, cleared, escalated), severity, customer_id, from_date, to_date, cursor, limit. Response 200: {alerts: AMLAlert[], next_cursor: string, total_count: integer}. GET /alerts/{alert_id} - Retrieve a specific AML alert. Response 200: Full alert object including triggered rules, transaction details, customer history summary, and analyst notes. PUT /alerts/{alert_id} - Update an AML alert (for compliance analyst review). Request body: {status: string, analyst_notes: string, reviewer_id: string}. Response 200: Updated alert object. Status transitions: open -> under_review -> cleared|escalated. Escalated alerts require filing a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR). Schemas. AMLAlert: {alert_id, txn_id, customer_id, rules_triggered, risk_score, severity, status, analyst_notes, created_at, reviewed_at, reviewer_id}. Rule: {rule_id, rule_name, description, severity, matched_pattern}. AML Rules. STRUCT-001: Structuring detection - Multiple transactions within 24 hours with individual amounts below $10,000 reporting threshold, total exceeding $10,000. RAPID-001: Rapid movement - Funds received and transferred out within 4 hours. GEO-001: High-risk geography - Transactions involving FATF-designated high-risk jurisdictions. MERCH-001: Unusual merchant - Transaction patterns inconsistent with declared merchant category.
